about.title: Santa Clarita Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product that fails should never become your burden to prove. In Santa Clarita, defective goods turn up in ordinary places: a space heater in a garage off Sierra Highway, a child's car seat on the drive down Mcbean Parkway, a power tool picked up for a weekend project near Bouquet Canyon Road. When something like that breaks and hurts you, California law treats it differently from a typical negligence case. Under strict liability, you generally need to show the product had a defect in its design, manufacturing, or warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. You do not have to prove the company was careless. Responsibility can also reach past the manufacturer to the distributor and the retailer that put the item in your hands. Records show 706 injury collisions in Santa Clarita for 2025, and some crashes trace back to tires, brakes, or airbags that did not perform as designed. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney for these claims, and you pay nothing unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: How LawProactive Helps With a Santa Clarita Product Claim

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: In California you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that anyone was negligent. An attorney in our network can help frame your claim around that standard from the start.

items.title: The Product Itself Is Evidence
items.desc: Keeping the failed item, its packaging, and any receipts can matter a great deal. We connect you quickly so an attorney can advise on preserving what you have before it is discarded or repaired.

items.title: More Than One Party May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the Santa Clarita retailer that sold the product may each share liability. An independent attorney can look at the full supply chain rather than stopping at the brand name on the box.

items.question: I threw away the broken product after I was hurt in Santa Clarita. Do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Losing the product makes things harder, but it does not automatically end a claim. Photos, receipts, medical records, the model number, and any remaining packaging can still help establish what failed and how. Talk with an attorney before assuming the case is gone, and stop discarding anything else connected to the incident.

items.question: My airbag or tire failed in a crash on Soledad Canyon Road. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. The other driver may be responsible for the collision, while the manufacturer of a part that did not perform as designed may be separately liable under strict liability. Santa Clarita logged 1,042 people injured in collisions during 2025, and some of those injuries involve equipment failures that deserve a closer look. An attorney can help sort out which claims apply to your situation.
